docs.title: Welcome to Stockflow Help
docs.text: Welcome to the official documentation and inspiration hub for Stockflow.media. Whether you're a filmmaker, designer, educator, or digital agency, our massive library of premium assets is designed to elevate your creative projects.

docs.title: 1. Welcome to Stockflow
docs.text:
Stockflow.media is a curated marketplace designed by artists for creators, social media managers, and filmmakers. We offer professional-grade 4K food and beverage assets in specific formats (16:9, 9:16, and 1:1) for a fraction of the cost of traditional stock sites.

The Best Part: No monthly subscriptions. Buy only what you need, when you need it.

docs.title: 2. Navigating the Marketplace
docs.text: Our interface is designed to be "Goldilocks" simple—not too much, not too little.

docs.title: The Header & Search
docs.text:
• Search Bar: Located at the top, you can search by title (e.g., "Pouring Coffee") or by tags (e.g., "Macro," "Slow Motion").

  • My Purchases (📜): Once signed in, this is your personal vault where you can re-download any asset you’ve previously licensed.

docs.title: Category Filters
docs.text:

docs.title: 3. How to Purchase & Download
docs.text: We use a Wallet-Based System to make checkouts instant and secure. 1. Sign In: Use your Google account for a one-click login. 2. Add Funds: Click "Add Funds" in the header. We offer top-up tiers powered by Stripe for 100% secure transactions. 3. Preview: Click any video card to open the High-Def Preview Modal. You can see the full resolution, tags, and license price here. 4. License & Download: Click "Download." The amount will be deducted from your wallet, and you will receive: - An instant high-res download link. - A confirmation email with the link. - A permanent copy in your "My Purchases" tab.

docs.title: Using 8K Images for Print Media
docs.text: When it comes to print — whether a magazine spread, a billboard, a restaurant menu, or an exhibition panel — image resolution is everything. Stockflow.media's collection of 8K resolution images provides the pixel density required for large-format, professional-grade printing at any scale.

docs.title: Why 8K for Print?
docs.text:
Standard digital images (72–150 PPI) look sharp on screen but break down in print. Professional print workflows demand:

  • 300 DPI at print size for sharp, gallery-quality output.
  • Lossless source files so editing and scaling doesn't degrade the result.

With an 8K image (7680×4320 pixels), you can print at full 300 DPI up to an area of approximately 65 cm × 36 cm (A1 size) — and at lower DPI for much larger formats like banners and murals, still with crisp detail.

docs.title: What You Can Print
docs.text: Format Size Recommended Use A4 Brochure 21×29.7 cm Restaurant menus, product sheets A2 Poster 42×59.4 cm Exhibition displays, in-store signage A0 Banner 84.1×118.9 cm Trade show back-walls, retail backdrops Custom Mural 2m+ wide Restaurant walls, corporate lobbies

docs.title: Print Workflow Recommendations
docs.text:
1. Download the highest resolution variant (8K / 7680×4320 or 7799×4254).
  2. Open in Adobe Photoshop or Affinity Photo.
  3. Set Image Resolution to 300 PPI (Image > Image Size — uncheck "Resample").
  4. Save as TIFF or PSD for handoff to a professional print shop, or as JPEG 100% for digital short-run printing.
  5. Always request a proof print before ordering large quantities.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Canva is used by over 170 million people worldwide to create social media graphics, presentations, posters, and educational content. Professional scientific imagery from Stockflow.media is fully compatible with Canva and can be imported directly into any project in seconds.

docs.title: Why Use Scientific Visuals in Canva?
docs.text:
Generic Canva templates produce generic results. Scientific visuals — microscopic cells, biological specimens, cinematic food photography — immediately make your content stand out and communicate depth and credibility.

Ideal for: - Science educators building engaging classroom content - Social media managers creating science fact posts - Healthcare brands building trust through authentic imagery - Academic institutions designing research posters and event materials - YouTube creators building Canva thumbnails for science channels

docs.title: Step-by-Step: Adding Stockflow Assets to Canva
docs.text:
1. Download your chosen asset from Stockflow.media — MP4 or JPEG
  2. Open your Canva project
  3. Click Uploads > Upload files > select your downloaded file
  4. Drag the asset onto your canvas
  5. Resize, reposition, and add text or other elements on top

Tip: For video backgrounds, upload the MP4 and set it as the page background. For image posts, use JPEG files — up to 8K for maximum sharpness.

docs.title: How to Use Stock Footage in Documentaries
docs.text: Documentary filmmakers demand authenticity, depth, and precision. Stockflow.media provides a curated library of premium stock footage — from microscopic biological animations to vibrant food culture visuals — that can transform your production without inflating your budget.

docs.title: Why Stock Footage Works in Documentaries
docs.text:
The best documentaries weave together original interviews and supporting B-roll to contextualise the story. Licensing every microscopic shot, time-lapse, or cultural food scene from scratch is prohibitively expensive. A premium stock library gives you:

  • Access to impossible shots — microscopic views of living cells, viral particles, and microorganisms that no single production team could recreate.
  • Consistent visual quality — all assets are 4K and 8K resolution, shot with professional colour grading in mind.
  • Immediate licensing — no usage negotiations, no clearance delays.

docs.text: Theme Collection Best Use Science & Biology Microscopic Cell close-ups, viral animations, organism behaviour Food Culture Food & Beverage Cultural dining, ingredient close-ups, cooking rituals

docs.title: Workflow Tips
docs.text:
1. Start with a shot list that identifies where B-roll is needed. Look for moments where narration describes something the camera cannot physically capture live.
  2. Browse by subcategory to find visually relevant clips quickly (e.g., "Biological Creatures" for a biology segment, "Food Menu" for a culinary episode).
  3. Download the 16:9 widescreen versions (3840×2160) for the best match to standard documentary deliverables.
  4. Use colour match tools in Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve to blend our footage seamlessly with your own camera work.

docs.title: SEO Tips for Documentary Creators
docs.text:
If you are distributing your documentary on YouTube or a website, using visually rich thumbnails derived from our high-resolution still frames can significantly boost click-through rates.

docs.title: Importing MP3 Files Into Your Project
Adobe Audition / Premiere Pro
docs.text:
1. Import the .mp3 file via File > Import.
  2. Drag it to the Audio Track on your timeline.
  3. Use the Essential Sound panel to set it as Ambient, Music, or SFX.

docs.text:
1. Drag the .mp3 directly into a GarageBand track.
  2. Use the Smart Controls panel to adjust EQ and reverb.

docs.text:
1. Open the Fairlight page.
  2. Import via the Media Pool and place on the timeline.
  3. Use bus routing for multi-track blending.

docs.title: Tips for Best Results
docs.text:
• Layer ambient audio underneath narration to add realism without overpowering the voice.
  • Use music stems to remove or highlight specific instruments when your visuals need more or less energy.
  • For social content, keep audio under -6 dBFS to avoid clipping on mobile devices.
  • All MP3 assets are royalty-free once licensed.

docs.title: Using PNG Images from Stockflow.media
docs.text: Browse Collections

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
PNG (Portable Network Graphics) is the standard format for images requiring transparency, precision, and lossless quality. PNG versions are available for select collections — ideal for layering, compositing, and design work.

Coming soon: Expanded PNG asset delivery with full transparency support across all collections.

docs.title: Why PNG for Creative Projects?
docs.text:
Unlike JPEG, PNG supports a transparent background (alpha channel) — meaning you can place the image over any colour, texture, or video without a white or coloured box around it.

This makes PNG the professional standard for: - Logo design — no background, scalable overlay on brand materials - Web UI elements — buttons, icons, overlays, illustrations - Compositing — layering imagery over video or presentation slides - Broadcast graphics — lower thirds, title cards, motion graphics

docs.title: How to Use Vector Files from Stockflow.media
docs.text: Stockflow.media's vector assets are ideal for designers, agencies, and developers who need infinitely scalable, lossless graphics. They can be resized to any dimension — from a small mobile icon to a full billboard print — without any quality loss.

docs.title: Supported Vector Formats
docs.text: Format Description Best For SVG Web-native, editable XML format Web design, UI/UX, interactive animations EPS Professional vector format Print design, magazine layouts, branding AI Adobe Illustrator native Complex multi-layer design work PDF Universal print-ready format High-fidelity print and press production

docs.title: Adobe Illustrator
docs.text:
1. Go to File > Open and select your vector file.
  2. Each element (shapes, lines, fills) is fully editable.
  3. Use Object > Expand to separate complex grouped elements.

docs.title: Figma
docs.text:
1. Drag and drop the SVG directly onto your canvas.
  2. All vector paths are automatically editable.
  3. Resize using the constraint handles without quality loss.

docs.title: Inkscape (Free & Open Source)
docs.text:
1. Use File > Open for SVG or EPS files.
  2. Use Object Properties to explore layer structure.

docs.title: For Print (InDesign / Affinity Publisher)
docs.text:
1. Place (Ctrl+D) the EPS or PDF into your layout.
  2. Scale freely — vector quality is resolution-independent at any print size.

docs.title: Tips for Best Results
docs.text:
• Always use SVG for web and screen; use EPS or PDF for professional print.
  • If exporting from Illustrator for the web, use Save As > SVG and enable "Embed Images" only if needed.
  • Vectors from our Microscopic and Food & Beverage collections work exceptionally well as stylised background elements or icon overlays.

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
• Scientific infographic backgrounds (microscopic illustrations)
  • Menu design for restaurants (food collection vectors)
  • Logo compositions and brand identity assets
  • Animated overlays for motion graphics (using SVG in After Effects)

docs.title: How to Use MP4 Video Footage from Stockflow.media
docs.text: Stockflow.media's MP4 video assets are professionally produced in resolutions up to 4K and 8K, making them ready for any production pipeline — from quick social media posts to full-length documentary films.

docs.title: Supported Resolutions & Aspect Ratios
docs.text:
Our MP4 footage is available in three standard aspect ratios:

Format Resolution Best For 16:9 Widescreen Up to 3840×2160 YouTube, TV, documentaries 9:16 Vertical Up to 2160×3840 Instagram Reels, TikTok, Shorts 1:1 Square Up to 2160×2160 Instagram Posts, Facebook

docs.title: Using MP4 Footage in Video Editors
Adobe Premiere Pro
docs.text:
1. Import the .mp4 file via File > Import.
  2. Drag the clip to your sequence timeline.
  3. Use Effect Controls to scale, mask, or colour grade.

docs.title: DaVinci Resolve
docs.text:
1. In the Media Pool, right-click and choose Import Media.
  2. Match your timeline resolution to the footage resolution for best results.
  3. Use the Color page for professional grade correction.

docs.title: Final Cut Pro
docs.text:
1. Import using File > Import > Media.
  2. Enable Optimised Media for smoother playback on large files.

docs.title: Tips for Best Results
docs.text:
• Do not re-compress unnecessarily. Export at the same codec and bitrate when possible.
  • For documentary overlays, use the 16:9 widescreen versions as B-roll on a lower opacity layer.
  • For social content, use the vertical 9:16 versions — they are pre-framed for mobile screens.
  • All clips are royalty-free once licensed. No attribution required.
